nodes.label: AppImage bundleMediaFramework
nodes.summary: Tauri's appimage.bundleMediaFramework gates whether the AppImage ships a GStreamer runtime at all. Set to false (the Tauri default) the linuxdeploy gstreamer plugin never runs, so no plugin .so, no AppRun hook, no rpath fixup; the bundled WebKitGTK then dlopens the host libgstreamer-1.0.so and uses the host registry. An AppImage has no other dependency mechanism, so there is no fallback.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c2-linux-packaging-deps [ses_f1acf8cbbffeBuLTWmhwQZ7M5F].md:L9422] - `appimage`: the only key present is `bundleMediaFramework: false`. No `files` map, no per-AppImage dep declaration (AppImages have no dependency mechanism at all).

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c2-linux-packaging-deps [ses_f1acf8cbbffeBuLTWmhwQZ7M5F].md:L9530] With `false`, **none** of that happens: no plugin `.so`s, no AppRun hook, no rpath fixups. Consequence: the AppImage's WebKitGTK dlopens the **host's** `libgstreamer-1.0.so` and uses the **host's** registry. On a host without GStreamer, the webview has no demuxer and no decoder; `<audio>` resolves but produces silence. (Separately, Tauri copies only `WebKitNetworkProcess`, `WebKitWebProcess` and `libwebkit2gtkinjectedbundle.so` from the webkit dir — it never bundles `libwebkit2gtk` itself, which is why the sysreq page tells AppImage users to install WebKitGTK manually.)

nodes.label: gstreamer1.0-plugins-base Ogg decode
nodes.summary: Ogg demux and Vorbis decode live in gstreamer1.0-plugins-base, not in plugins-good. The element that actually needs plugins-good is autoaudiosink. Because gstreamer1.0-plugins-good hard-depends on gstreamer1.0-plugins-base, a deb that names only plugins-good is transitively adequate for Ogg/Vorbis, so the exposure is the AppImage rather than the deb dependency list.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c2-linux-packaging-deps [ses_f1acf8cbbffeBuLTWmhwQZ7M5F].md:L9455] **So the "in `plugins-good`" premise is wrong.** Ogg demux + Vorbis decode are `plugins-base`; the thing that actually needs `plugins-good` is `autoaudiosink`. Because `gstreamer1.0-plugins-good` depends on `gstreamer1.0-plugins-base` (measured analogue: Arch `gst-plugins-good` `Depends On: gst-plugins-base-libs=1.28.7-2 …`), the deb is **transitively** adequate for Ogg/Vorbis. The real risk is not the deb — it is the AppImage, which has no dependency resolution whatsoever.

nodes.label: Declaring libasound2 in deb.depends is unsatisfiable on Debian 13 trixie and Ubuntu 24.04+
nodes.summary: Snipset's tauri.conf.json declares Depends: libasound2. Debian 13 trixie ships libasound2t64 and the plain libasound2 binary only exists up to bookworm/noble-23, so the dependency cannot be satisfied and the .deb fails to install. The fix is libasound2t64 with libasound2 as an OR fallback; the Arch equivalent is alsa-lib. This is a hard install failure, not a subtle audio fault, and the contract test only asserts that depends is defined and non-empty, so no test catches it.

nodes.label: The Rust audio path uses rodio and cpal and never touches GStreamer
nodes.summary: engine/audio.rs play_raw_ogg decodes the shipped .ogg cues in-process with rodio::Decoder and outputs through rodio::DeviceSinkBuilder to cpal (ALSA/JACK on Linux). GStreamer is not involved, so those cues and the TTS playback keep working on a host with zero GStreamer installed. That makes "no sound at all on Linux" overstated, and it makes the failure signature partial: webview click sounds, the Pomodoro music player, chat voice messages and YouTube audio all go silent while the Rust-side sound_snippet.ogg still plays.
nodes.norm_label: the rust audio path uses rodio and cpal and never touches gstreamer
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c2-linux-packaging-deps [ses_f1acf8cbbffeBuLTWmhwQZ7M5F].md:L9547] - `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/engine/audio.rs:107-123` — `play_raw_ogg` reads `sound_snippet/toggle/clipboard/theme_*` `.ogg` and decodes **in-process** with `rodio::Decoder`, outputs via `rodio::DeviceSinkBuilder` → `cpal` (ALSA/JACK on Linux). **GStreamer is not involved.**

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c2-linux-packaging-deps [ses_f1acf8cbbffeBuLTWmhwQZ7M5F].md:L9558] **Concretely:** on an AppImage-only user with no GStreamer installed, **every webview UI click sound, the Pomodoro music player, chat voice messages, and YouTube audio are silent**, while the Rust-side `sound_snippet.ogg` / TTS cues still play. That "half the app is silent" signature is a strong fingerprint for this defect.

nodes.label: ERROR: logging before google.Init is a glog severity prefix on INFO lines, not an error
nodes.summary: The Antigravity CLI installer prints every one of its progress lines with an "ERROR: logging before google.Init" prefix. google.Init has not run yet, so glog falls back to stderr and prefixes each line; the payload after the colon starts with I, which is INFO. The install succeeded and nothing is broken. The prefix is baked into the shipped binary, so there is nothing to fix in the installation.
nodes.norm_label: error: logging before google.init is a glog severity prefix on info lines, not an error
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - fixing-antigravity-cli-installation-errors [ses_f177e3d27ffeKsA7Jw5IfgZj8N].md:L408] 2. **The "ERROR: logging before google.Init" lines are NOT errors.** They are glog (Google's logging library) messages. `google.Init` hasn't run yet, so glog falls back to stderr and prefixes every line with "ERROR: logging before google.Init". The content inside (`I0928 ...` = Info level) is INFO, not error. Purely cosmetic log noise from Google's own installer code.

nodes.label: The Antigravity installer placed its ~/.local/bin PATH export after the interactive guard in .bashrc
nodes.summary: The installer appended `export PATH="/home/.../.local/bin:$PATH"` to the end of .bashrc, i.e. after the `[[ $- != *i* ]] && return` guard on line 12. A non-interactive login shell `bash -lc` sources .bashrc through .bash_profile, the guard returns, and .local/bin is dropped from PATH; measured before the change: bash -lc 1, bash -c 0, bash -ic 2. Removing the installer block during cleanup regressed bash -lc from 1 to 0. The fix is one pre-guard export of ~/.local/bin with .local/bin dropped from the post-guard line 53, which gives exactly one occurrence in all three cases and closes the pre-existing bash -c gap as well.
nodes.norm_label: the antigravity installer placed its ~/.local/bin path export after the interactive guard in .bashrc
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - fixing-antigravity-cli-installation-errors [ses_f177e3d27ffeKsA7Jw5IfgZj8N].md:L1390] Now the proper fix: put `.local/bin` export **before the interactive guard** in `.bashrc`. That gives 1 in all three cases, and closes the pre-existing `bash -c` gap too (which matches the user's own comment at lines 5-6: "Environment untuk SEMUA shell (harus sebelum guard interaktif di bawah, supaya shell non-interaktif milik agent/skrip ikut dapat)").

nodes.label: ~/.gemini/config/ is the Antigravity global customization root
nodes.summary: Antigravity resolves skills, rules and MCP servers from four locations in priority order: workspace .agents/ walking up to the repo root, declared skills.json/plugins.json, the global configuration root, then built-in customizations mounted by name. The global root is ~/.gemini/config/, so global skills are ~/.gemini/config/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and the global MCP registry is ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json. The session verified this against the built-in agy-customizations docs rather than assuming it.

nodes.label: Antigravity caps each rule file at 24,000 bytes and truncates on line boundaries
nodes.summary: Each GEMINI.md / AGENTS.md is capped at 24 KB (24,000 bytes) measured after @[label](path) includes are expanded, and over-cap files are truncated on line boundaries rather than rejected. Always-on and global rules share a separate 20,000-token budget, over which rules are demoted to file-path pointers. The WSL backup GEMINI.md is 32,286 bytes, so importing it verbatim would have been silently truncated and had to be trimmed to 13,037 bytes.

nodes.label: Converting the backed-up SKILL.md.docx to markdown with markitdown destroys the YAML frontmatter
nodes.summary: The WSL backup stores every skill as SKILL.md.docx. markitdown renders the YAML frontmatter as a markdown heading instead of a frontmatter block, so `name:` and `description: |` end up inside one `## name: ... description: ...` line. A `Trigger:` key with colon-space is then an illegal plain YAML scalar, and backslash escapes such as ctx\_doctor and <PLUGIN\_ROOT> survive into the body. Converting is lossy, which is why the already-repaired OpenCode copies were used for cross-checking instead.
